Let E be the full finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure and canonical full-space Lebesgue/Haar volume, including dimension zero. The approved ambient instances belong to the contract; E is a connected real vector space and the full-space volume is nonzero.
Let u:E->R be locally integrable with respect to this volume. Assume that for every real C1 compactly supported test psi:E->R and every direction a:E, the actual function x->u(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) is volume-integrable and
  integral u(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx = 0.
Then there exists ONE real c such that u(x)=c for volume-almost every x in E.
Local integrability is ordinary volume-local L1, not a global-volume L1 requirement. The derivative is the genuine real Frechet derivative of the C1 test function, not a totalized zero derivative asserted for the rough u. The same c works on the whole space, not a separately chosen value on each neighborhood/test/direction; c may depend on u. The conclusion is an almost-everywhere equality, not pointwise constancy or classical differentiability of u. No mollifier, sequence, or derivative certificate is an input. No disconnected-domain analogue, uniqueness assertion, weighted operator-domain converse, spectral gap or additional functional inequality is an explicit conclusion.

Let E be the full finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel space with its canonical full-space volume, including dimension zero and all approved ambient instances. Let W:E->R be C1 and assume exp(-W) is integrable against volume. Define mu=volume.tilted(x->-W(x)), the actual normalized Gibbs measure exp(-W)/integral exp(-W) times volume. In this full-space setting the approved context gives the positive normalized density; no separate positive-partition hypothesis is a displayed binder in this statement.
For every real-linear partial operator D:L2(mu;R)->L2(mu;E), assume D is closable and its graph is characterized exactly as follows: for every scalar L2 class a and vector L2 class H, (a,H) belongs to D.graph iff there exists a smooth compactly supported real function phi:E->R with a=phi mu-almost everywhere and H=gradient(phi) mu-almost everywhere. D.closure is the genuine single-valued operator from that same graph closure, with its actual submodule domain.
Then for every u in this SAME D.closure.domain, if D.closure(u)=0 as an actual vector L2(mu) class, there exists a real c with (u as a scalar L2(mu) representative)(x)=c for mu-almost every x.
D is fixed before every u. The constant c is selected after u and may depend on u; no universal common constant for all zero-output elements is claimed. The premise is equality of the true closed-gradient output to the zero vector quotient, not a claim that the rough representative's totalized derivative vanishes pointwise. C1 regularity of W suffices here and no curvature, positive spectral gap, dense-domain condition or mean-zero assumption is added. This is a universal implication for a supplied closable exact-gradient D, not an existential construction of D. It is one direction only: zero output implies weighted-AE constancy. It does not produce constant-function domain membership or prove full kernel equality, nor a centered/epsilon-zero/range/Poincare or further inequality/core/composition theorem. There is no joint measurable choice of constants.

Let E be the full finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel space with canonical full-space volume, including dimension zero and all approved section ambient instances. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta:NNReal and eta:R. Assume alpha cast to R is strictly positive, alpha<=beta, V is C2, and for every x,a:E both exact actual Hessian bounds hold:
  alpha*||a||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x a) a,
  (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x a) a <= beta*||a||^2.
Assume eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Define actual measures and reflected potential
  mu=volume.tilted(x->-V(x)),
  J=map((x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g),mu.prod(stdGaussian E)),
  W_y(z)=V((y+z)/2)+||z-y||^2/(8*eta).
Tilted means the actual exp(-potential)/partition density against volume; standard Gaussian, independent product and pushforward are genuine measures.
There exist kernels R,S:E->Measure E with all the following simultaneous properties: R and S are Markov kernels; R disintegrates the swapped actual joint J.map Prod.swap; and for every y:E,
  S(y)=(R(y)).map(x->2*x-y).
For every y:E, S(y)=volume.tilted(z->-W_y(z)), W_y is C2, exp(-W_y) is volume-integrable and its volume integral strictly positive. For this y there exists a real-linear partial operator D:L2(S(y);R)->L2(S(y);E) with dense domain in the scalar L2 space, D closable and D.closure closed. Its original graph is exactly characterized by: for every scalar L2 class a and vector L2 class H, (a,H) belongs to D.graph iff there exists a smooth compactly supported real function phi with a=phi S(y)-almost everywhere and H=gradient(phi) S(y)-almost everywhere.
For every u in this SAME D.closure.domain, if D.closure(u)=0 as an actual vector L2(S(y)) class, there exists a real c such that the scalar quotient's standard representative equals c S(y)-almost everywhere.
One common R,S pair is chosen before all y. For each y one original D is chosen before ALL of its closure-domain u; a suitable D is not chosen afresh for each u. The constant c may depend on y and u and is selected after them. Potential/density/operator conclusions hold for every y, not only almost every y. The conditional-kernel property has its usual disintegration/version scope, not a claim that all possible conditional versions have these pointwise identities. All unannotated partition integrability/integrals use volume; graph and zero-output constancy use actual weighted quotient classes and AE under S(y). No rough classical derivative or Hessian is asserted. No joint measurable y-dependent operator/constant selector, constant-domain converse or full kernel equality, resolvent estimate, centered/epsilon-zero/range/Poincare or further inequality, core/main or expected-cost composition theorem is concluded.
